public_rationale: The historical comparison holds: document-based question answering was documented in Watson in 2011. The characterization of contemporary autonomous agents is too narrow. WebVoyager already selected and executed browser actions before the post. Its incomplete success rate supports caution about usefulness, but does not reduce its capabilities to document question answering.
limitations: A research agent does not establish the quality of every commercial product.
Successful browser interaction does not establish a dependable general personal assistant.
The older and newer systems share a question-answering capability, not necessarily an architecture.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: So-called autonomous agents are effectively chatbots answering questions from documents, a decade-old technology.

statement.excerpt: Every single story about artificial intelligence seems to begin with “well, AI can’t do much yet, but…” and then lean into sloppy science fiction that masks that these “autonomous agents” are effectively chatbots that can answer questions based on a document, tech that’s existed for a decade or more.

from_speaker: effectively chatbots that can answer questions based on a document
tech that’s existed for a decade or more
our_interpretation: The central capability claim is that contemporary autonomous agents amount to document question answering, without materially broader action-taking capabilities.
The historical comparison separately asserts that document-based question answering existed by May 2014.
The target covers technology history through publication because the statement explicitly combines contemporary capabilities with a decade-or-more comparison; it supplies no earliest historical date.
The rhetorical claim about every news story is outside the supplied normalized proposition.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary agent systems are limited to document question answering, and dated records establish that this capability existed at least ten years earlier.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous agents demonstrably select and execute actions beyond document question answering, or the asserted historical age is disproved. Opposing results for the two components warrant mixed.

evidence.explanation: WebVoyager observes websites, chooses actions and executes them through a browser, with an evaluation reporting 55.7% task success in this original version. Those interactive capabilities exceed answering questions from a supplied document, even though reliability was incomplete.

evidence.locator: Opening explanation of question answering, following the abstract
evidence.publisher: Association for Logic Programming; Adam Lally and Paul Fodor
evidence.explanation: The authors describe Watson's February 2011 system deriving answers using unstructured text and matching evidence from passages. This establishes the document-question-answering capability more than a decade before the post, without establishing equivalence to modern agent architectures.
